questions.prompt: Does the liquid conduct electricity (well enough to light a bulb)?
questions.explain: Solutions of salts, acids and bases contain ions and conduct; sugar water, oil and pure water don't.

questions.prompt: Why does salt water conduct electricity but sugar water does not?
options: Salt forms ions (charged particles) in water; sugar does not
questions.explain: Ions carry the current through the liquid.

questions.prompt: In copper plating, the object to be plated is connected to the…

feedback.0: Positive copper ions are attracted to the NEGATIVE terminal.

questions.explain: The object is the negative electrode (cathode), where copper deposits.

questions.prompt: Match each plating to its purpose.

pairs.right: Looks like gold at low cost

questions.explain: Electroplating combines a cheap, strong base metal with a useful surface.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of copper-plating an iron key in order.
steps: Connect the key to the negative terminal and a copper plate to the positive
Dip both into copper sulfate solution
Switch on the current for some time
Remove the key: it has a copper coating
questions.explain: Clean → connect correctly → electrolyte → current → coated key.

questions.prompt: During copper plating, the copper sulfate solution stays blue. Why?
options: The copper plate (anode) dissolves and replaces the copper ions that deposit on the key
questions.explain: Copper leaves the anode as ions at the same rate as copper deposits on the cathode.

questions.text: A liquid that conducts electricity and is changed by it is an ___. The rods dipped into it are called ___.
questions.explain: Electrolyte = conducting liquid; electrodes = the metal rods.

questions.prompt: In the lab, what happened when you SWAPPED the wires so the key was on the positive terminal?
options: No copper deposited (existing coating was removed)
questions.explain: Positive copper ions are repelled by a positive electrode, so no plating happens there.

questions.prompt: Why is it dangerous to touch electrical switches with wet hands, even though pure water is a poor conductor?
questions.modelAnswer: Water on our hands is not pure: it contains dissolved salts (from sweat, tap water or dirt), which form ions. This makes it a good conductor, so electricity can flow through the water and our body, causing an electric shock.
rubric: The water on hands is not pure / contains dissolved salts
Current could pass through the body, causing a shock
questions.explain: Real-world water almost always contains ions.
